 Oral Judgment

(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum) The captioned appeal is by the
claimants
questioning the quantum and negligence of 50% attributed to the deceased, who was riding a bike.
The insurance company admits its liability.
Therefore, the appeal is purely on quantum and negligence.

2. Fact leading to the case are as under:
The appellants filed a claim petition in MVC No.528/2016 for having lost one Timmareddy in a road traffic accident dated 23.11.2016.
The claimants contend that Timmareddy was proceeding on a bike at about 7-30 p.m.
The driver of the offending car who had illegal parked the vehicle on the middle of the road without parking lights was directly responsible for the accident and which led to death of Timmareddy.
3. The claimants contended that the deceased was working as a coolie and agriculturist and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
The Tribunal while answering issue No.1 referring to the charge sheet material, held that the rider of the bike has also contributed to the accident.
Therefore, by fixing the negligence of 50% on the deceased and 50% on the driver of the offending car, the Tribunal proceeded to determine the quantum.
While determining loss of dependency, the Tribunal notionally assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- and awarded Rs.13,32,732/- under the head of loss of dependency.
The Tribunal, in all awarded Rs.14,02,700/-.
5. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants/claimants and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.3/insurance company.

Finding on negligence:
6. The materials in the charge sheet unequivocally establish that the driver of the offending vehicle had negligently parked the car in the middle of the road, thereby obstructing the natural flow of traffic.
A particularly noteworthy aspect of this situation, which NC: 2024:KHC-K:9547 merits careful consideration by the Court, is the location where this act of illegal parking occurred.
The offending vehicle was stationed on a curved section of the road, a spot inherently hazardous for road users due to limited visibility and the reduced reaction time it affords to oncoming traffic.

This act of parking at such a precarious location not only posed a significant danger but also further compounded the risks for other drivers and road users approaching from the same direction,
increasing the likelihood of accidents.
The Tribunal only on the assumption that even the rider of the bike was charge sheeted, has proceeded to fix 50% negligence.
Merely because there is collision between two vehicles, that in itself will not constitute contributory negligence.

sentences.text: Oriental
Insurance
Company Limited and Others1 held that presumption in regard to accident is against the persons parking the vehicle in the middle of the road.
Two factors (2018) 3 SCC 365 NC: 2024:KHC-K:9547 are relevant in the case on hand.
Firstly, the driver of the offending car could not have parked the vehicle in the middle of the road that too at 7-30 p.m.
Secondly, the place where the car was parked, the charge sheet material clearly reveal that there is curve.
These two factors led to a presumption that the rider of the bike had no occasion to sight the offending car which was illegally parked on the middle of the road.

Therefore,
finding of the Tribunal that the rider of the bike also contributed to the accident is not only perverse but contrary to the charge sheet material and the law laid down by the Apex Court in the above cited judgment.

Having regard to the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that entire negligence has to be attributed on the driver of the offending car who had illegally parked the car on the middle of the road.
Therefore, finding on negligence is reversed.
The entire negligence is fastened on the driver of the offending car.

NC: 2024:KHC-K:9547 Finding on quantum :
7.
Though the claimants have asserted that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, no documentary evidence is adduced to substantiate the income of the deceased.
Though the Tribunal was justified in notionally assessing the income of the deceased, however, the income notionally assessed at Rs.7,000/- appears to be marginally is on the lower side.

In absence of income proof,
this Court is inclined to place reliance on the income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident is of the year 2016.
Accordingly, the income is notionally assessed at Rs.8,750/-.
If 40% is added towards future prospects, the income is assessed at Rs.12,250/-.

After deducting 1/3rd of the income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, the income is assessed at Rs.8,167/- and by applying a multiplier of 17, the compensation payable under the head of loss of dependency works out to Rs.16,66,068/-.
Under conventional heads, the claimants are entitled for Rs.1,50,000/- as there are three dependents.

The accident is of the year 2016 and applying the principles laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi2, 10% escalation is awarded for every three years on conventional heads which works out to Rs.30,000/-.

sentences.text: The total compensation re-determined by this Court works out to Rs.18,46,068/- as against Rs.14,02,700/-.

9. In the light of findings recorded supra, this Court passes the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.4,43,368/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The enhanced amount shall be apportioned in terms of the judgment rendered by the Tribunal.
